issues.reason: A place-name pre-nominal modifier is exactly the gap the reviewer itself registers, and the remedy it cites — the Brindle-estuary mapping to (Member birmingham office) — would assert the city IS an office, a falsehood, whereas (LocatedIn sk_office_1 birmingham) is true, well-typed containment traceable to the word 'Birmingham', so the calibration line licenses the improvisation.

'ready to go' is an infinitival, not a PP, complement, so the adjective-PP rule the reviewer cites does not reach it (its own gap 3), and the parser used the nearest licensed machinery — the control-verb pattern's tenseless top-level complement attached by Theme with the controller copied in as Agent — with everything sealed under say's Theme, so nothing is asserted.

Wrapping an entity-attached preposition-named oblique in the clause's tense is explicitly licensed by 'There was a ledger on the workbench.' -> (Past (On sk_ledger_1 sk_workbench_1)), so the Past wrapper is not confined to Member/Inheritance/PartOf.

gaps_confirmed: direct quotation as a speech verb's complement — only finite that-clauses are covered by the attitude rule
'the <Placename> N' where the proper noun locates rather than names the referent ('the Birmingham office')
an adjective with an infinitival complement ('ready to go') — the complement rule covers PP arguments only
a vague duration adjunct with no number or unit ('for some time') — Measure/MeasureAtLeast both need a magnitude
new_gaps: a predicative appositive ('Dahle, a spokesman for the office') yields only a Member atom, so the appositive noun has no symbol for its PP complement to attach to; the Complements-of-nouns rule presumes a noun symbol and the parse has to hang (For …) on the person instead
a direct quotation's surface wording has no carrier — string literals are reserved for Name facts — so the quoted form is lost even when the content is correctly sealed
notes: All three issues are gap-territory objections to improvisation that emits nothing false, ill-typed or over-asserted; the continuative perfect (Ongoing, no Past), the seal's definite projection and the past-host appositive wrapper are all handled per the instruction set.
